markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize one inexpensive, falsifiable model change: a recent-history residual added to SASRec’s final representation. Retain it as the first experiment; no improvement is established, and stronger recency can also reinforce unsuitable substitutes.

**Insights and directions.**

1. User feedback favors recent behavior and repeated narrow preferences. Test recency explicitly without claiming to recover intent, ownership, compatibility, or purchase necessity.
2. Current probes measure sampled training separation and embedding alignment. Neither establishes validation ranking quality; preserve official macro HR@10 for selection.
3. Missing metadata and empty batches weaken diagnostics. Return unavailable values with counts, restore model mode, and use only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions.
4. Shuffling studies question whether benchmarks require sequence order [1]. Simple temporal controls are warranted, but an unweighted recent mean is invariant to permutations within its selected window.
5. Reproducibility findings show configuration-dependent architecture comparisons [2]. Freeze one checkpoint per dataset and change one scoring component initially.
6. Sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog rankings [3]. Keep the pinned evaluator authoritative; label full-catalog observations separately.
7. SASRec’s tied embeddings make the residual an item-similarity score mixture [5]. Raw embedding norms and popularity may explain gains, so improvements alone would not establish better current-intent modeling.

These insights suggest three directions: simple recency modeling, controlled sensitivity diagnostics, and explicit uncertainty about unobserved product relationships.

**Framework.**

| Component | Observable evidence | Supported conclusion | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| SASRec | Ordered interactions | Learned sequence associations | Current intent |
| Recent-item mean | Last observed interactions | Recent similarity signal | Purchase necessity; norm/popularity effects |
| Perturbation probes | Paired output changes | Sensitivity to history | Causal explanation |
| Title/specification audit | Explicit text spans | Documented relationships | Ownership and compatibility when unspecified |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-history residual [1,2,5] | 3/6/3 | Cheap, direct test of recency | Familiar mixture; may amplify satisfied needs or popularity |
| Matched recent/older removal probes [1] | 4/7/3 | Tests reliance on history regions | Removal changes positions and length |
| Abstaining specification audit [4] | 6/6/6 | Makes evidence inspectable | Sparse specifications limit coverage |
| Matched similarity/popularity controls [6,7] | 3/7/4 | Separates recency from generic score effects | Additional tuning increases budget and selection optimism |

**Selected algorithm.** Let `h` be SASRec’s final valid-position feature and `m` the mean of the last `min(5, history_length)` raw, nonpadding item embeddings. Score candidate `i` as `h·e_i + alpha*(m·e_i)`. Divide by the actual interaction count; return zero for empty histories. Include neither positional vectors nor input lookup `sqrt(d)` scaling, and apply no normalization after addition. Final LayerNorm does not make `h` unit length [5].

Freeze the trained checkpoint and select a separate scalar per dataset from `alpha ∈ {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2}` using pinned validation HR@10, breaking ties toward zero. Independent category selection maximizes the separable macro objective but permits 256 joint configurations; these are not independent trials. Including zero retains the baseline. All comparisons consume the shared budget.

```python
for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    model = load_baseline_checkpoint(dataset).eval()
    for alpha in [0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2]:
        scores = score_raw_recent_residual(model, alpha, recent_count=5)
        save_pinned_validation_user_hits(dataset, alpha, scores)
    save_selected_alpha_and_checkpoint(dataset, tie_break="smallest_alpha")
```

Persist checkpoint revision, configuration, mappings, selected alpha, candidate identities, and per-user hits. Update the predictor writer with identical scoring and retain all four routes, seeds, splits, `SASREC_EPOCHS=200` environment default, and `DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']`.

Prespecify any follow-up ablations: last-item, full-history, matched random-five and oldest-five similarity; popularity-only and candidate-norm-only additions. Give variants identical tuning opportunities and score calibration; treat cosine scoring, normalized history embeddings, signed weights, and timestamp effects as separate experiments. Do not expand this grid adaptively without logging the additional search.

Report per-dataset feature/residual/candidate norm quantiles, cosine alignment, relative residual magnitude, relative candidate-score spread, score correlation, and top-10 changes. Undefined ratios must remain unavailable. Bootstrap paired user hits within each dataset for 10,000 replicates and report the macro improvement’s 95% percentile interval. This conditions on fixed models and candidates and does not correct winner selection [8,9]. Selection-aware in-bag/out-of-bag resampling can diagnose optimism, but cannot remove adaptive-search bias [10].

Retain `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` and `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`. Apply the residual independently to every causal prefix, restore model mode, and return `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. Keep full-catalog diagnostics and the twenty-user simulator separate from official selection. Compatibility and already-satisfied needs remain hypotheses, not observed labels.

References: [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.03873), [3](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651), [4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7075849/), [5](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py), [6](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling), [7](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.04276), [8](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html), [9](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [10](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.07180).

idea.description: Add a validation-selected recent-history embedding residual to each dataset’s frozen SASRec representation, with explicit raw-embedding semantics and matched controls for recency, popularity, and embedding norms.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback identifies insufficient emphasis on recent, specific behavior. A small additive residual tests whether recent item similarity adds predictive value beyond SASRec, while alpha=0 retains baseline scoring. Any gain remains evidence about pinned sampled-candidate HR@10, rather than proof of improved intent understanding, compatibility, or purchase necessity.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, unchanged splits, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment default 200. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Freeze one baseline checkpoint per dataset before residual selection; record how each checkpoint was selected and every subsequent validation query. Use raw item_emb.weight lookups, without sqrt(d) scaling or positional embeddings, and apply no normalization after adding the residual. Average the last min(5, valid_prefix_length) nonpadding interactions using their actual count; empty prefixes yield zero. Verify padding rows, masks, left/right alignment, truncation, and final valid-position extraction against the pinned baseline implementation. Cache baseline and residual candidate scores in evaluation mode and retain the pinned evaluator’s ranking and tie behavior. Choose alpha from {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2} per dataset, breaking equal-HR ties toward smaller alpha. Raw alpha is not comparable across datasets because feature and candidate norms differ. Save checkpoint revision, architecture/configuration, mappings, alpha, recent_count, residual semantics, fixed candidate identities, and per-user validation hits; update the predictor writer to reproduce the same scores. Verify exported scores against training-side inference on identical observed prefixes and candidate IDs. Adapt view.log2feats and view.predict_score so diagnostics include the residual exactly once, with causal last-five means at each position. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), view.model as the actual nn.Module, the compatibility fields, and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions. Restore the original model training mode in finally; return null with valid counts and a reason for empty or undefined measurements. Do not use unavailable categories or reviews. For diagnostics use epsilon=1e-8 for determining undefined norms or score standard deviations; report undefined ratios/cosines as null rather than fabricating finite values. Report norm and alignment quantiles, alpha*||m||/||h||, alpha*std(m·e)/std(h·e), candidate-score correlation, top-10 overlap, and category-specific HR before macro averaging. A paired bootstrap uses seed 42, 10,000 replicates, and 200 resampled users independently per dataset, reusing indices across compared models; compute macro hit differences and percentile intervals. These intervals exclude checkpoint/weight-selection optimism, training-seed variability, and negative-sampling variability. If selection-aware resampling is run, repeat the actual recorded checkpoint/weight selection in each in-bag sample and assess it on out-of-bag users; label this an exploratory selection diagnostic, especially after adaptive searches. Subsequent controls must have prespecified equal tuning opportunities and calibration. Keep cosine scoring and normalized-history variants separate because they alter score geometry. Positive versus negative similarity and timestamp effects are follow-up hypotheses, not part of the initial grid. Preserve the twenty-user full-catalog simulator and distinguish its qualitative feedback from official selection. No exact frozen-SASRec-mixture benefit is established by the cited sources. The baseline implementation is not supplied, so this remains an implementation specification rather than an executable replacement train.py.
idea.pseudocode:
ALPHAS = (0.0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2)
K = 5

def causal_recent_mean(sequence, raw_item_embeddings, k=K):
    # For every B x L position, select only nonpadding events at or before it.
    # Keep the last k events, preserve observed repetitions, and divide by
    # their actual count. Empty prefixes return the zero vector.
    return last_k_valid_prefix_means(sequence, raw_item_embeddings, k)

def residual_features(sequence, baseline_features, item_emb, alpha):
    m = causal_recent_mean(sequence, item_emb.weight)
    # Raw embeddings: no sqrt(d), positions, or post-addition normalization.
    return baseline_features + alpha * m

for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    model = load_frozen_baseline_checkpoint(dataset).eval()
    sequences, candidates = pinned_validation_inputs(dataset)
    with no_grad():
        h = final_valid(model.log2feats(sequences), sequences)
        m = final_valid(causal_recent_mean(sequences, model.item_emb.weight), sequences)
        base_scores = candidate_dot(h, model.item_emb, candidates)
        residual_scores = candidate_dot(m, model.item_emb, candidates)
        hits = {}
        for alpha in ALPHAS:
            scores = base_scores + alpha * residual_scores
            hits[alpha] = pinned_evaluator_user_hits(scores, candidates)
            save_user_hits_and_diagnostics(dataset, alpha, hits[alpha], h, m, scores)
    best_alpha = max(ALPHAS, key=lambda a: (mean(hits[a]), -a))
    save_trial_artifacts(model, best_alpha, K, residual_semantics='raw_no_postnorm')
    write_predictor_with_identical_scoring(dataset, best_alpha, K)
    verify_exported_score_parity_on_observed_prefixes(dataset)

# Selection score: arithmetic mean of four selected category HR@10 values.
# Paired uncertainty: resample users independently within each category,
# using the same indices for baseline and selected model; average four
# category hit differences. Fixed-winner intervals do not correct selection.
# Diagnosis uses the same residual for every causal prefix, exactly once.

originality.positive: The proposal connects an explicit recency hypothesis to a tightly controlled SASRec score decomposition and auditable diagnostics.
originality.negative: Recent embedding averages and additive score mixtures are established techniques; benchmark-specific controls provide methodological value rather than a new model principle.

future_potential.positive: A cheap initial experiment can identify whether recent pairwise similarity warrants further temporal or evidence-based modeling.
future_potential.negative: Benefits may reflect norms, popularity, or sampled-candidate selection and may leave compatibility and satisfied needs unresolved.

code_difficulty.positive: The initial model change needs only a causal masked mean, a scalar, cached score mixtures, and matching exported inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable padding handling, position-wise diagnostic parity, artifact persistence, uncertainty reporting, and controlled ablations require more work than the original rating implied.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? An Analysis of Datasets for Evaluation of Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Uses interaction shuffling to examine whether benchmark performance depends on sequence order.
Motivates simple temporal controls and matched perturbation diagnostics.
limitations: Shuffling sensitivity does not establish users’ true intent or explain individual recommendation errors.
Permuting items inside an unweighted averaging window cannot change that residual.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation reproducibility study
contributions: The supplied summary reports that SASRec versus GRU4Rec comparisons depend strongly on configuration and parameter count.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed recent-history residual improves these four datasets.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model-order reversals.
limitations: Does not provide grounds for replacing the task’s pinned evaluator.
Pinned sampled-candidate improvements cannot automatically be interpreted as full-catalog improvements.

related_work.title: Snorkel: Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision
contributions: Provides labeling functions that vote or abstain and methods for combining noisy supervision.
limitations: Heuristic product audits need separate validation and cannot establish compatibility when evidence is missing.
Only permitted titles and descriptions can support metadata-based rules in this task.

related_work.title: Original SASRec implementation
contributions: Documents scaled input embeddings, final normalization, and scoring with the tied item embedding table.
Supports the algebraic decomposition of the proposed residual into baseline scores plus recent-item embedding similarity.
limitations: The pinned RecHarness implementation must be checked for its own masking, scaling, and normalization choices.
Implementation algebra does not demonstrate empirical improvement.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: The supplied summary compares Transformer models with last-item and recency-weighted pairwise models, including popularity adjustment.
Motivates testing simple temporal and popularity controls.
limitations: Does not establish benefits from mixing frozen SASRec embeddings.
Reported benchmark results do not guarantee transfer to this task.

related_work.title: NISER: Normalized Item and Session Representations with Graph Neural Networks
contributions: Studies representation normalization and the relationship between embedding norms and popularity bias in session recommendation.
limitations: Uses a session-based graph setting rather than frozen SASRec.
Normalization changes the scoring function and requires a separate controlled variant.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling, supporting reuse of user indices across compared models.
limitations: The four-category macro statistic requires explicitly stratified user resampling.
Fixed-model bootstrap intervals do not correct validation-based model selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimization of a noisy selection criterion produces selection bias.
limitations: Does not quantify optimism for this exact search without additional measurements.
A bootstrap interval around the selected winner does not remove the bias.

related_work.title: Bootstrap Bias Corrected Cross Validation Applied to Super Learning
contributions: Motivates repeating selection within bootstrap samples and assessing selected configurations out of bag.
limitations: Applying this approach to fixed validation hit matrices is a diagnostic adaptation.
It cannot fully correct adaptive candidate generation driven by the same validation labels.
